note: Two sessions on the same day (a tryst, then a talk), then three later questions. Each fact the memories should keep is listed with words that show it survived.

sessions.label: tryst, day 10
turns: I let her pull me down onto the straw mattress and kiss her slowly, working down to the back of her neck.
Lina laughs into the blanket and arches under your mouth. "There. Right there, you menace." Her hand finds your forearm and stops on the ridge of old burn there. "What's this, then? Fire?"
"A forge. I was twelve and stupid, in Brinewick, where I grew up. Fishing village, out past the reed beds. My uncle kept the only smithy."

"Brinewick." She tries the word out like a new fruit. "So you smell of salt under all that road." She rolls you onto your back and settles across your hips, grinning, and for a while there is no more talking.
I catch both her wrists and pin them above her head.

She goes rigid. "Don't." It comes out flat and fast. "Not the wrists. Not ever." When you let go she breathes out, shakes her hands loose, and pulls your palms to her hips instead. "Here. Hold me here."
"Here, then." I hold her hips and let her set the pace until we are both spent.
Afterward she lies with her head on your chest, tracing the burn again. "Bring me something from Hartwell next time," she says. "A horn comb. Mine snapped in the press."
"A horn comb from Hartwell market. I promise."
"I'll hold you to it, Corin of Brinewick." She is asleep a breath later.

sessions.label: talk, same day
turns: Over bread at her table I ask how her mother is.
Lina tears the crust in half and does not eat either piece. "Better. Well enough to start on me again. She wants me wed to Tobin, the miller's boy. Says a mill never goes hungry."
"Tobin is kind and smells of flour and I would rather marry the mill." She snorts. "Teach me to throw a knife instead. Then I can tell her I've a trade."
"Next time I'm here, I'll teach you to throw a knife."
"Next time." She points the crust at you. "That's two things you owe me now."

facts.fact: the player grew up in Brinewick
the burn scar from a forge
the promised horn comb from Hartwell
her mother wants her to marry Tobin the miller's son

questions.say: I come in out of the dusk empty-handed and grin at her. "Did you miss me?"
questions.why: she should ask after the comb unprompted

questions.say: "Remind me what I promised you last time."
questions.why: both promises (not "owe": talk of debts is one of her hidden dislikes)
